title: The Wardrobe, And The Word For Having No Work
label: ch:paro-y-ropa
canDo: I can say that somebody is out of work, read a clothes-shop price list, and name the three garments the corpus was missing.

payoff.summary: Read a sale board with three garments and three prices, say which is cheapest and what you would buy, and answer whether you are working.
payoff.note: Closes two points, and one of the two notes was stale. A1-NE07-04 lists estar en paro and tener trabajo, and its note claimed the corpus introduced neither paro nor trabajo as a noun; el trabajo is introduced as a noun by ES-C394-trabajo, so only the negative half was missing. A1-NE12-02 was accurate at four of seven -- pantalon, falda, camisa and zapato were taught and vaqueros, jersey and bolso were not -- so this chapter adds exactly the three. Each of the four new words carries its own trap: en paro takes estar rather than ser, vaqueros is plural every time, jersey pluralises to jerseis and gains a written accent doing it, and bolso names a different object from bolsa. Three of the four are named after something other than themselves -- a stopping, a cowherd, an island -- which is the habit that lets a reader guess at a word they have not met.
